name: deepV12
description: 12 m offshore deep-V speedboat: the ONE set of defining numbers for the physics proxy (src/speedboat/hullMesh.ts) and the render hull (Blender). Physics builds its mesh from `spec`; `stations` is the generator's output at the proxy's own stations, pinned equal by tests/hullWater.test.ts.
frame: hull frame: x across the beam (symmetric, +x one side), y up from the keel baseline, z forward from the transom (z = 0 at the transom, z = loa at the stem)

scaling.law: mass, LCG, VCG and inertia DERIVED from `massItems` (deriveMassProperties); geometry set by concept sign-off: 12 m LOA, 24 deg deadrise, chine beam 2.30 m, deck height kept at 1.674 m
scaling.check: overall beam with 8 deg flare over the top 0.71 m of topside = 2.50 m, inside the 2.44-2.51 m of real 12 m deep-Vs (Cigarette 38 Top Gun: 11.43 m, 2.44 m beam, 24 deg, 4.49 t dry with twin sterndrives)

propPoint.note: centreline EQUIVALENT of the three drives (physics thrust point); per-engine points in `engines`

derived.sides: vertical from chine to deck in the physics proxy (flare is render-only)
derived.stem: forefoot at z = 11.65 (keel length), deck-level stem at z = 12: rake 0.35 m, modelled in the proxy (STYLE-SPEC C4)
derived.deadrise: 24 deg constant aft of z 7.2 m (60% LOA), warping (t^2) to 45 deg at the forefoot; per-station values in `stations[].deadriseDeg` (STYLE-SPEC C8). Sources: Sport Fishing Mag "Perfect Boat Hull Designs" (Regulator 24 deg transom to 48-49 deg forward); Ray Hunt Design deep-V Q&A (deadrise varies continuously). Savitsky uses the TRANSOM (constant, prismatic) deadrise: 24 deg

engines.model: Mercury Racing 450R V8 (4.6 L), 689 lb dry — ethanol variant assumed same mass
engines.propNote: propeller disc 0.55 m aft of the mounting plane (under the aft third of the 0.86 m cowl — ASSUMED from the cowl proportions) and 0.22 m below the anti-ventilation plate; plate 0.10 m above the keel line on the 30 in setback bracket: planing boats run the plate flush to 1/2 in above the bottom, a bracketed outboard ~2 in higher because the prop runs in the hump behind the hull (TwoMorrow Holdings/Boat Builder Central, 'Outboard shaft lengths and transoms', 2016); setback rules of thumb give +1 in per 4–10 in of setback (+3 to +7.5 in at 30 in; boating forums). The prop disc spans the keel line: partly surface-piercing at speed, as Mercury Racing's Sport Master gearcase is designed to run

lowerUnit.note: Steering gearcase of each outboard as a low-aspect-ratio lateral foil (physics only; per-engine position from `engines[].mountX` / `mountZFromTransom`). ALL NUMBERS ASSUMED from the 30 in bracket and the prop point above: no gearcase drawing. Mercury Racing publish a 5.44 in (0.138 m) HD offshore torpedo; strut chord and skeg depth are typical-looking, not measured.
lowerUnit.steerAxisNote: the drive yaws about a vertical axis through the mount point (mountX, mountZFromTransom); steer + rotates the thrust line from body +z toward body +x
lowerUnit.areaNote: strut 0.22 m (plate to prop shaft) x 0.30 m chord + torpedo 0.55 m x 0.138 m (5.44 in HD offshore) + skeg 0.25 m x 0.18 m = 0.19 m2; span plate to skeg tip 0.50 m, geometric AR = 0.50^2/0.19 = 1.3; centre of area 0.21 m below the plate, mid-gearcase 0.35 m aft of the mount. ASSUMED proportions (no drawing)
lowerUnit.shaftNote: 450R shaft lengths 20/25/30 in (Boating Mag 450R review); shaft length = clamp to anti-ventilation plate (TwoMorrow Holdings 2016); 30 in XXL on the bracket

renderOnly.note: Features below the physics proxy's resolution. The proxy does NOT model them; values are ASSUMED typical, not from a drawing.
renderOnly.strakesPhysics: NOT in the physics proxy (5 cm flats are far below its 286-triangle resolution). Implication: real strakes stop the spray root at the first dry strake, so the Wagner splash-up width the proxy uses for the spray-root wetted area (friction) and for the 2D+t c may run wider than the real boat once c passes a strake; a strake-capped c is the proxy-side change if friction or lift reads high
